raw.translational: Understanding the distinct roles of COL7A1 and TRAPPC10 in cellular protein handling highlights potential therapeutic avenues. While COL7A1 defects primarily affect extracellular matrix, TRAPPC10 defects impact intracellular trafficking, suggesting that therapeutic strategies might need to be tailored to the specific cellular compartment and process affected. However, shared pathways in protein processing could offer broader targets for intervention in conditions with related molecular underpinnings.

raw.translational: Understanding the potential overlap in ECM processing pathways affected by both COL7A1 and TRAPPC2 could reveal novel therapeutic targets for connective tissue disorders. If TRAPPC2 indirectly influences ECM component secretion, strategies to modulate this could benefit patients with COL7A1-related disorders, and vice versa, by targeting common downstream pathways.

partners.mechanism_chain: COL7A1 (HGNC:2206) —DISRUPTS→ Type VII collagen processing and secretion (GO:0031011); Type VII collagen processing and secretion (GO:0031011) —LEADS_TO→ ECM organization (GO:0030198); ECM organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ Nail dysplasia (HP:0001071); NSF (HGNC:7794) —DISRUPTS→ Vesicular transport (GO:0006888); Vesicular transport (GO:0006888) —LEADS_TO→ ECM organization (GO:0030198); Vesicular transport (GO:0006888) —LEADS_TO→ Global developmental delay (HP:0001263); Vesicular transport (GO:0006888) —LEADS_TO→ Seizures (HP:0001250). Loss-of-function mutations in COL7A1 impair the processing and secretion of type VII collagen, a key component of the dermal-epidermal junction, leading to nail dysplasia. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in NSF disrupt vesicular transport, essential for protein trafficking and secretion, including components of the ECM. This disruption in vesicular transport indirectly affects ECM organization, contributing to both nail defects and neurological phenotypes such as global developmental delay and seizures.

partners.mechanism_chain: COL7A1 (HGNC:2207) —LEADS_TO→ Nail dysplasia (HP:0000957); COL7A1 (HGNC:2207) —DISRUPTS→ Unfolded Protein Response (GO:0034960); Unfolded Protein Response (GO:0034960) —INCREASES→ ER-associated degradation (GO:0006584); SAR1B (HGNC:10131) —DISRUPTS→ Unfolded Protein Response (GO:0034960); SAR1B (HGNC:10131) —LEADS_TO→ Intestinal malabsorption (HP:0002045); SAR1B (HGNC:10131) —LEADS_TO→ Fatty diarrhea (HP:0030169). Loss-of-function mutations in COL7A1 (causing nonsyndromic congenital nail disorder 8) and SAR1B (causing chylomicron retention disease) both converge on the dysregulation of the Unfolded Protein Response (UPR) and ER-associated degradation (ERAD) pathways. COL7A1 is essential for collagen fibril formation and extracellular matrix integrity, and its dysfunction can lead to cellular stress and activation of the UPR. SAR1B is critical for COPII vesicle formation, essential for ER to Golgi transport; defects in SAR1B lead to ER stress and accumulation of misfolded proteins, activating the UPR and ERAD. Both pathways are involved in cellular quality control and can lead to downstream phenotypic consequences when disrupted.

partners.mechanism_chain: TRAPPC9 (HGNC:20075) —DISRUPTS→ TRAPP complex function in ER-Golgi transport (GO:0006893); TRAPP complex function in ER-Golgi transport (GO:0006893) —LEADS_TO→ keratin filament organization (GO:0030244); keratin filament organization (GO:0030244) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability, autosomal recessive 13 (MONDO:0013173); COL7A1 (HGNC:2298) —DISRUPTS→ Nonsyndromic congenital nail disorder 8 (MONDO:0011852). Loss-of-function mutations in TRAPPC9 disrupt its function in ER-Golgi transport, which in turn affects keratin filament organization, leading to intellectual disability. Separately, COL7A1 mutations cause nonsyndromic congenital nail disorder 8. The proposed overlap is the shared role of TRAPPC9 in cellular processes that indirectly influence keratin structures, which are also critical for nail formation. Thus, disruptions in keratin filament organization due to TRAPPC9 dysfunction could manifest in both neuronal and ectodermal (nail) tissues.
